claims.text: The starting material is a high-entropy alloy in a solid-solution state.
Creating a high-entropy alloy introduces lattice distortion.
High-entropy alloys contain chemical disorder arising from a random arrangement of constituent atoms.
The randomly arranged atoms have differing masses and sizes.
Lattice distortion and chemical disorder increase phonon scattering.
The increased phonon scattering reduces phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
The high-entropy alloy will have lower phonon thermal conductivity than traditional alloys or compounds.
The proposed effect applies at room temperature and atmospheric pressure.
The proposed effect should hold from 300 K to 1000 K.
The proposed effect should hold from atmospheric pressure to 10 GPa.
Grain size and defects may affect the relationship between lattice distortion, phonon scattering, and thermal conductivity.

contradictions.description: The starting material is already described as a high-entropy alloy, while the intervention is described as creating a high-entropy alloy; this does not define a distinct treatment applied to an untreated starting alloy.
The conditions restrict the hypothesis to room temperature and atmospheric pressure, whereas the boundary expands it to 300–1000 K and pressures up to 10 GPa.
